# Construct the sequence T designed to maximize overlap (near arithmetic progression)
# We need 87 elements (t_0 to t_86). t_86 - t_0 = 171. 86 gaps.

# We place the single gap of 1 at the end for maximal initial uniformity.

# t_0 up to t_85 (86 elements) are mostly arithmetic progression with difference 2
for i in range(86):
    T.append(2 * i)

# t_86 is the final element

# Verify constraints

# Calculate the sum set S = { t_i + t_j | 0 <= i <= j <= 86 }

N = len(T)
for i in range(N):
    for j in range(i, N):
        sum_set.add(T[i] + T[j])

# Report the size of the sum set

def calculate_sum_set_size(t):
    """Calculates the number of distinct elements in the sum set {t_i + t_j | 0 <= i <= j < len(t)}."""
    sums = set()
    N = len(t)
    for i in range(N):
        for j in range(i, N):
            sums.add(t[i] + t[j])
    return len(sums)

# Case N=4

The size of the sum set $|S|$ is minimized when the elements of $T$ are structured most closely to an arithmetic progression (AP). If $T$ were a perfect AP of size $N$, the resulting sum set $S$ would be a contiguous sequence of integers, and its size would be exactly $2N-1$.
